# Terraform MCP server reference

This page contains reference information about the Terraform MCP server, including configuration options and tools.

## Available tools

The Terraform MCP server provides specialized tools that AI models can use to access current Terraform registry information. These tools work automatically when you ask relevant questions, you don't need to invoke them manually.

## Toolsets 

The server includes the following toolsets:

| Toolset | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `registry` | Tools for accessing the public registry |
| `registry-private` | Tools for accessing private registries |
| `terraform` | Tools for interacting with HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise |

You can add the `--toolsets` flag to enable or disable these tools when starting the binary.

You can add the `--tools` flag instead to enable individual tools by name. You cannot use the `--tools` flag together with the `--toolsets` flag. Refer to [Command-line flags](#command-line-flags) for more information.

### Provider tools

Access comprehensive provider documentation for resources, data sources, functions, and configuration guides.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `search_providers` | Find provider documentation by service name | List of available documentation with IDs, titles, and categories |
| `get_provider_details` | Retrieve complete documentation for a specific provider component | Full documentation content in markdown format |
| `get_provider_capabilities` | Discover all resource types a provider supports before looking up specific resources | List of resources, data-sources, function names and more |
| `get_latest_provider_version` | Retrieve the latest version of a specifc provider | The latest version of a provider |

Example prompt: "How do I configure an AWS S3 bucket with versioning enabled?"

### Module tools

Discover and explore community and verified modules from the Terraform registry.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `search_modules` | Find modules by name or functionality | Module details including names, descriptions, download counts, and verification status |
| `get_module_details` | Get comprehensive module information | Complete documentation with inputs, outputs, examples, and submodules |
| `get_latest_module_version` | Retrieve the latest version of a specific module | The latest version of a module |

Example prompt: "Show me modules for deploying a Kubernetes cluster on AWS."

### Policy tools

Access Sentinel policies for governance and compliance requirements.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `search_policies` | Find Sentinel policies by topic or requirement | Policy listings with IDs, names, and download statistics |
| `get_policy_details` | Retrieve detailed policy documentation | Policy implementation details and usage instructions |

Example prompt: "What Sentinel policies are available for enforcing security best practices?"

### Private registry tools

Find private modules and providers in your HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise organization. These tools belong to the `registry-private` toolset.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `search_private_modules` | Find private modules in your organization | List of private modules matching search criteria |
| `get_private_module_details` | Get detailed private module information | Complete module details including inputs, outputs, and examples |
| `search_private_providers` | Find private providers in your organization | List of private providers matching search criteria |
| `get_private_provider_details` | Get detailed private provider information | Provider details including usage and version information |

### Identity and organization tools

Identify the authenticated token and list the organizations that the token can access. These tools belong to the `terraform` toolset.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `whoami` | Identify the user or service account that the Terraform token belongs to | Username, email address, and whether the token belongs to a service account |
| `get_token_permissions` | Get the permissions for the `TFE_TOKEN` | A list of actions you can take |
| `list_terraform_orgs` | Fetch all Terraform organizations | List of organizations with their details |

### Project tools

Manage projects in an organization. These tools belong to the `terraform` toolset.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_terraform_projects` | Fetch all Terraform projects | List of projects with their metadata |
| `create_project` | Create a project in an organization | Details of the created project |
| `get_project` | Fetch detailed information about a project by its ID | Project details including name, description, and default execution mode |
| `delete_project` | Delete a project by ID. The request fails when the project still contains workspaces or Stacks. `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` must also be set to `true`. | Confirmation of deletion |

### Team tools

Manage teams and team access in an organization. These tools belong to the `terraform` toolset.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_teams` | List teams in an organization, with optional filters for exact team names or a search query | Summary of each team including ID, name, visibility, and member count |
| `get_team` | Fetch full details for a single team by ID | Team details including members, organization access permissions, and SSO settings |
| `create_team` | Create a team in an organization | Team ID, name, and visibility |
| `add_team_member` | Add a single member to a team by username or organization membership ID | Confirmation that the member was added |
| `grant_team_access` | Grant a team access to a workspace or a project | The created access grant including its ID, team ID, target resource ID, and access level |
| `delete_team` | Permanently delete a team by ID. `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` must also be set to `true`. | Confirmation of deletion |

### Workspace tools

Manage workspaces in an organization. These tools belong to the `terraform` toolset. Some tools require the `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` environment variable for destructive operations.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_workspaces` | Search and list workspaces in an organization | Workspace details including configuration and status |
| `get_workspace_details` | Get comprehensive workspace information | Complete workspace configuration, variables, and state information |
| `create_workspace` | Create a new Terraform workspace. | Confirmation of workspace creation (destructive operation) |
| `create_no_code_workspace` | Create a workspace from a no-code module. The tool uses MCP elicitation to collect the required module variables from you. | Details of the created workspace |
| `update_workspace` | Update workspace configuration. | Updated workspace configuration (potentially destructive) |
| `delete_workspace_safely` | Delete workspace if it manages no resources. `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` must also be set to `true`. | Confirmation of deletion |
| `force_unlock_workspace` | Force unlock a workspace that is stuck in a lock. Requires workspace admin permissions. `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` must also be set to `true`. | Confirmation that the workspace is unlocked |

### Run, plan, and apply tools

Create runs and inspect their plans, applies, and comments. These tools belong to the `terraform` toolset.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_runs` | List or search runs in a workspace | Run details with optional filtering |
| `get_run_details` | Get detailed information about a specific run | Complete run information including logs and status |
| `get_run_comments` | List the comments that users submitted on a run | ID and body text of each comment |
| `create_run` | Create a new Terraform run | Run creation confirmation with available run types |
| `action_run` | Perform apply, discard, or cancel operations on runs. `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` must also be set to `true`. | Action confirmation |
| `get_plan_details` | Fetches detailed metadata about a specific Terraform plan | Plan metadata |
| `get_plan_logs` | Retrieves the execution logs of a specific Terraform plan | Plan logs as text |
| `get_plan_json_output` | Retrieves the structured JSON output of a Terraform plan, providing detailed resource changes in a machine-readable format that is easier to parse than plain logs | Plan output in JSON format |
| `get_apply_details` | Fetches detailed metadata about a specific Terraform apply | Apply metadata |
| `get_apply_logs` | Retrieves the execution logs of a specific Terraform apply | Apply logs as text, or a status message when the apply is still in progress |
| `get_sentinel_mock` | Export and download Sentinel mock bundle data for a plan | Sentinel mock data that you can use to test policies against plan output |

### State version tools

Inspect the state versions of a workspace. These tools belong to the `terraform` toolset.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_state_versions` | List the state versions of a workspace | Summary of each state version including ID, creation time, serial, and Terraform version |
| `get_state_version` | Retrieve a specific state version, or the latest state version of a workspace | State version details |

### Policy set tools

Read and attach the policy sets for a workspace. These tools belong to the `terraform` toolset.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_workspace_policy_sets` | Get the policy sets attached to a particular workspace | A list of policy sets |
| `attach_policy_set_to_workspaces` | Attach a policy set to a workspace | Confirmation of attachment |

### Variable management tools

Manage variables and variable sets across workspaces and organizations.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_variable_sets` | List all variable sets in an organization | Variable set details and configurations |
| `create_variable_set` | Create a new variable set | Confirmation of variable set creation |
| `create_variable_in_variable_set` | Add a variable to a variable set | Variable creation confirmation |
| `delete_variable_in_variable_set` | Remove a variable from a variable set | Variable deletion confirmation |
| `attach_variable_set_to_workspaces` | Attach variable set to workspaces | Attachment confirmation |
| `detach_variable_set_from_workspaces` | Detach variable set from workspaces | Detachment confirmation |
| `list_workspace_variables` | List all variables in a workspace | Workspace variable details |
| `create_workspace_variable` | Create a variable in a workspace | Variable creation confirmation |
| `update_workspace_variable` | Update an existing workspace variable | Updated variable configuration |

### Workspace tagging tools

Manage tags for Terraform workspaces to organize and categorize resources.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `create_workspace_tags` | Add tags to a workspace | Tag creation confirmation |
| `read_workspace_tags` | Read all tags from a workspace | List of workspace tags |

Example prompts:
- "Create a new workspace called 'production-app' in my organization"
- "Show me all runs for the staging workspace"
- "List all private modules related to AWS"
- "Create a variable set for database configuration"

### Stacks tools

Manage Terraform Stacks in an organization.

| Tool | Purpose | What it returns |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `list_stacks` | Retrieve list of stacks | List of stacks with high level summary |
| `get_stack_details` | Read full details for a specific stack | Full stack configuration |

Example prompts:
- "List all the stacks in my organization"
- "Show me the details for the `dev-environment` stack"


## Available resources

The Terraform MCP server provides several static read-only guides to the MCP clients to retrieve structured, contextual data. It helps generate standardized Terraform code. 

| Resource URI | Kind | Description |
|--------------|------|-------------|
| `/terraform/style-guide` | Resource | Provides access to the official Terraform style guide documentation in markdown format |
| `/terraform/module-development` | Resource | Comprehensive guide covering module composition, structure, providers, publishing, and refactoring best practices |
| `/terraform/providers/{namespace}/name/{name}/version/{version}` | Resource Template | Dynamically retrieves detailed documentation and overview for any Terraform provider by namespace, name, and version |

## Transport protocols

You can set one of the following transport protocols when starting the MCP server so that it operates correctly for your environment. 

|   Transport      |   Best for                                                      |   How it works                                                                                |   Usage                                                          |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `stdio`          | Local development and direct integration with MCP clients       | Uses standard input/output for JSON-RPC message communication                                 | Automatically used when no specific transport mode is configured |
| `streamableHTTP` | Remote deployments, distributed setups, production environments | HTTP-based transport with support for both direct HTTP requests                               | Enable by setting `TRANSPORT_MODE=streamable-http`               |

## Command-line flags

You can add the following flags when you start the server binary.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--toolsets` | Comma-separated list of toolsets to enable. Valid values are `registry`, `registry-private`, `terraform`, and `all`. |
| `--tools` | Comma-separated list of individual tool names to enable. When you set this flag, only the tools you name are available. You cannot use this flag together with the `--toolsets` flag. |
| `--log-file` | Path to the log file. |
| `--log-level` | Log level. Valid values are `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`, and `panic`. The default is `info`. The `LOG_LEVEL` environment variable overrides this flag. |
| `--log-format` | Log format. Valid values are `text` and `json`. The default is `text`. The `LOG_FORMAT` environment variable overrides this flag. |

You can add the following flags when you start the server with the `streamable-http` command.

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--transport-host` | Host to bind the HTTP server to. The default is `127.0.0.1`. |
| `--transport-port` | Port that the HTTP server listens on. The default is `8080`. |
| `--mcp-endpoint` | Path for the streamable HTTP endpoint. The default is `/mcp`. |
| `--heartbeat-interval` | Heartbeat interval for HTTP connections, such as `30s`. The default is `0`, which disables the heartbeat. |
| `--organization-allowlist` | Comma-separated list of HCP Terraform organization names that can access the HTTP server. The `MCP_ORGANIZATION_ALLOWLIST` environment variable takes precedence over this flag. |

## Health endpoint

In streamable HTTP mode, the server exposes a `/health` endpoint that returns a JSON response with the following fields.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Health status of the server. The value is `ok`. |
| `service` | Name of the service. The value is `terraform-mcp-server`. |
| `transport` | Transport protocol. The value is `streamable-http`. |
| `endpoint` | Path of the streamable HTTP endpoint. |
| `version` | Version of the running server. |

## Environment variables

You can set the following environment variables to configure the server behavior.

| Variable                       | Description                                                                  | Default                      |
|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| `TFE_ADDRESS`                  | HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise address                                | `"https://app.terraform.io"` |
| `TFE_TOKEN`                    | Terraform Enterprise API token                                               | `""` (empty)                 |
| `TFE_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY`          | Skip HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise TLS verification                  | `false`                      |
| `TRANSPORT_MODE`               | Set to `streamable-http` to enable HTTP transport (legacy `http`)            | `stdio`                      |
| `TRANSPORT_HOST`               | Host to bind the HTTP server. Set to `0.0.0.0` to bind to all interfaces                                                 | `127.0.0.1`                  |
| `TRANSPORT_PORT`               | HTTP server port                                                             | `8080`                       |
| `MCP_ENDPOINT`                 | HTTP server endpoint path                                                    | `/mcp`                       |
| `MCP_SESSION_MODE`             | Session mode: `stateful` or `stateless`                                      | `stateful`                   |
| `MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`          | Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS                             | `""` (empty)                 |
| `MCP_CORS_MODE`                | CORS mode: `strict`, `development`, or `disabled`                            | `strict`                     |
| `MCP_RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL`        | Global rate limit (format: `rps:burst`)                                      | `10:20`                      |
| `MCP_RATE_LIMIT_SESSION`       | Per-session rate limit (format: `rps:burst`)                                 | `5:10`                       |
| `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS`         | Enable destructive Terraform operations                                      | `false`                      |
| `MCP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL`       | Keep-alive long lived streamable HTTP connections (`0` to disable)           | `0`                          |
| `OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED`         | Enable tools metrics using OpenTelemtry                                      | `false`                      |
| `OTEL_METRICS_SERVICE_NAME`    | Identifies the source of the metrics                                         | `terraform-mcp-server`       |
| `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORT_INTERVAL` | Controls the frequency of metric flushes                                     | `2s`                         |
| `OTEL_METRICS_ENDPOINT`        | OpenTelemetry collector endpoint                                             | `localhost:4318`             |
| `LOG_LEVEL`                    | Logging level: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`, `panic`   | `info`                       |
| `LOG_FORMAT`                   | Logging format: `text` or `json` (overrides `--log-format` flag)             | `text`                       |
| `OTEL_METRICS_SERVICE_VERSION` | Server version that the metrics report                                       | The server version           |
| `INSTANA_ENABLED`              | Set to `true` to enable Instana instrumentation for the streamable HTTP server | `false`                    |
| `INSTANA_SERVICE_NAME`         | Service name that the server reports to Instana                              | `terraform-mcp-server`       |
| `MCP_TLS_CERT_FILE`            | Path to the TLS certificate file for the HTTP server                         | `""` (empty)                 |
| `MCP_TLS_KEY_FILE`             | Path to the TLS key file for the HTTP server                                 | `""` (empty)                 |
| `MCP_ORGANIZATION_ALLOWLIST`   | Comma-separated list of organization names that can access the HTTP server   | `""` (empty)                 |
| `MCP_FORWARD_CLIENT_IP`        | Set to `true` to forward the client IP address in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | `false`                    |
| `MCP_REMOTE_IP_METHOD`         | Method the server uses to determine the client IP address. Valid values are `RemoteAddr`, `X-Real-IP`, and `X-Forwarded-For`. | `RemoteAddr` |
| `MCP_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS`         | Number of trusted proxy hops, counted from the right of the `X-Forwarded-For` chain. Applies only when `MCP_REMOTE_IP_METHOD` is `X-Forwarded-For`. | `0` |
| `MCP_REDIRECT_ROOT_URL`        | URL that the HTTP server redirects requests for the `/` path to              | `""` (empty)                 |
| `TF_MCP_SHARED_SECRET`         | Shared secret that the server sends in the `X-Tf-Mcp-Secret` header on requests to HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise | `""` (empty) |

## Run type options

The `create_run` tool supports the following run types by default:

- `plan_and_apply`: Creates a plan and applies it if approved
- `refresh_state`: Refreshes the state without making changes
- `plan_only`: Creates a plan without applying
- `allow_empty_apply`: Allows applying when no changes are detected

When you set `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` to `true`, the following additional options become available:

- `auto_approve`: Automatically approves and applies the plan
- `is_destroy`: Creates a destroy plan to remove infrastructure

### Destructive operations

Several tools perform destructive operations that can modify or delete infrastructure resources. These tools are disabled by default and require setting `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS=true`:

- `action_run`: Can apply or destroy infrastructure
- `delete_workspace_safely`: Permanently deletes workspaces
- `force_unlock_workspace` force unlocks a workspace that is stuck in a lock
- `delete_project` deletes a project
- `delete_team` permanently deletes a team
- Additional run type options in `create_run`

<Warning>

When enabled, use these tools with caution as they can permanently modify or destroy infrastructure resources.

</Warning>

## Telemetry metrics

When enabled, the Terraform MCP server collects the following metrics:

| Type | Emitted metrics | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard HTTP server metrics | <ul><li>`http.server.request.body.size`</li><li>`http.server.response.body.size`</li><li> `http.server.request.duration`</li></ul> |  The server wraps the HTTP mux with `otelhttp.NewHandler(...)` to emit the metrics. |
| Custom tool metrics | <ul><li>`mcp_tool_calls_total`</li><li>`mcp_tool_errors_total`</li><li>`mcp_tool_duration_seconds`</li></ul> |  The server uses MCP hooks to call the `BeforeCallTool` and `AfterCallTool` tools, which emit the metrics. |
| Client metrics | <ul><li>`mcp_client_type_total`</li></ul> | The server counts connections by the name and version of the MCP client. |

When you set `INSTANA_ENABLED` to `true`, the streamable HTTP server also sends metrics and HTTP request traces to Instana.
